Tacos al Pastor

35 min (+30 min marinate)MediumServes 1–4

Prep — Marinated Pork on the Trompo

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Pork shoulder, thin-sliced120g240g360g480g
Achiote (annatto) paste15g30g45g60g
Dried guajillo chiles1234
Pineapple juice30ml60ml90ml120ml
White vinegar10ml20ml30ml40ml
Garlic cloves1234
Ground cumin⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Dried oregano⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Fresh pineapple, diced30g60g90g120g
White onion, diced20g40g60g80g
Corn tortillas36912
Cilantro, chopped5g10g15g20g
Lime wedges1234

Steps

  1. Soak the dried guajillo chiles in boiling water 15 minutes until soft, then drain and remove stems and seeds.
  2. Blend the softened chiles with achiote paste, pineapple juice, vinegar, garlic, cumin, and oregano until smooth.
  3. Coat the pork slices in the marinade and refrigerate at least 30 minutes.
  4. Heat a skillet with a little oil over medium-high until shimmering.
  5. Sear the pork in a single layer 3-4 minutes per side until deeply browned.
  6. Chop the cooked pork into bite-sized bits.
  7. In the same pan, caramelize the diced pineapple 1-2 minutes until golden-spotted.
  8. Stir the chopped pork back in with the pineapple for 30 seconds.
  9. Warm the corn tortillas about 20 seconds per side in a dry pan.
  10. Pile the pork and pineapple onto warm tortillas, topped with onion, cilantro, and lime.

Chicken Enchiladas Verdes

45 minMediumServes 1–4

Prep — Shredded Poached Chicken

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Chicken breast120g240g360g480g
Tomatillos100g200g300g400g
Jalapeño½11½2
Garlic cloves1234
White onion20g40g60g80g
Chicken stock60ml120ml180ml240ml
Cilantro5g10g15g20g
Corn tortillas2468
Vegetable oil (for tortillas)5ml10ml15ml20ml
Mexican crema or sour cream15ml30ml45ml60ml
Shredded Oaxaca or Monterey Jack cheese20g40g60g80g
Queso fresco, crumbled10g20g30g40g

Steps

  1. Poach the chicken breast in gently boiling water 12-15 minutes until no pink remains.
  2. Shred the cooled chicken into thin strips with two forks.
  3. Husk and rinse the tomatillos, then boil with jalapeño and garlic 8-10 minutes until soft and olive-green.
  4. Blend the tomatillos, jalapeño, garlic, onion, and cilantro until smooth into a salsa verde.
  5. Simmer the salsa with the chicken stock 5 minutes until slightly darkened.
  6. Preheat the oven to 190°C (375°F).
  7. Warm each tortilla in a little oil 5 seconds per side until pliable.
  8. Fill each tortilla with shredded chicken, roll tightly, and place seam-side down in a baking dish.
  9. Pour the salsa verde over the enchiladas, top with cheese, and bake 15-20 minutes until bubbling.
  10. Drizzle with crema and crumbled queso fresco before serving.

Pozole Rojo (Pork & Hominy Soup)

75 min (mostly hands-off)EasyServes 1–4

Prep — Hominy for the Pot

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Pork shoulder, cubed130g260g390g520g
White hominy (canned, drained)130g260g390g520g
Dried guajillo chiles1234
Dried ancho chile½11½2
Garlic cloves1234
White onion20g40g60g80g
Dried oregano⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Bay leaf¼½¾1
Shredded cabbage (garnish)20g40g60g80g
Sliced radish (garnish)10g20g30g40g
Lime wedges1234

Steps

  1. Simmer the pork with a quarter of the onion, a garlic clove, and the bay leaf, skimming foam, 45-60 minutes until fork-tender.
  2. Toast the stemmed, seeded chiles in a dry pan about 30 seconds per side until fragrant.
  3. Soak the toasted chiles in boiling water 15 minutes until soft.
  4. Blend the softened chiles with the remaining onion, garlic, and oregano, using soaking water to loosen. Strain.
  5. Lift the tender pork out, shred or chop it, and discard the bay leaf.
  6. Stir the strained red chile sauce into the broth.
  7. Return the pork and hominy to the pot and simmer uncovered 20 minutes.
  8. Taste and season with salt.
  9. Ladle into bowls and set out cabbage, radish, and lime for topping.

Chiles Rellenos

45 minMediumServes 1–4

Prep — Charring the Poblano Peppers

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Poblano peppers1234
Oaxaca or Monterey Jack cheese30g60g90g120g
Eggs, separated1234
All-purpose flour15g30g45g60g
Crushed tomatoes60g120g180g240g
White onion, chopped15g30g45g60g
Garlic clove½11½2
Chicken stock30ml60ml90ml120ml
Vegetable oil (for frying)60ml120ml180ml240ml

Steps

  1. Char the poblano peppers directly over a flame or under a broiler until blackened all over, about 8-10 minutes.
  2. Steam the charred peppers in a covered bowl 10 minutes, then rub off the blackened skin.
  3. Slit each pepper, scoop out the seeds and membrane, and stuff with cheese.
  4. Simmer the onion and garlic in oil 2-3 minutes, then add crushed tomatoes and stock, simmering 10 minutes for the sauce.
  5. Beat the egg whites to soft peaks, then gently fold in the yolks to make a fluffy batter.
  6. Roll each stuffed pepper in flour, then dip and coat fully in the egg batter.
  7. Fry the battered peppers in hot oil 3-4 minutes, turning gently, until golden and puffed.
  8. Drain on paper towels.
  9. Spoon the warm tomato sauce onto plates and top with a chile relleno to serve.

Tinga de Pollo (Smoky Chipotle Chicken Tostadas)

30 minEasyServes 1–4

Prep — Chipotle Peppers in Adobo

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Chicken breast120g240g360g480g
White onion30g60g90g120g
Garlic cloves1234
Roma tomatoes1234
Chipotle peppers in adobo½11½2
Adobo sauce (from the can)5ml10ml15ml20ml
Chicken stock30ml60ml90ml120ml
Tostadas (or corn tortillas)2468
Avocado¼½¾1
Queso fresco, crumbled10g20g30g40g
Shredded lettuce15g30g45g60g

Steps

  1. Poach the chicken in gently boiling water 12-15 minutes until no pink remains, then shred with two forks.
  2. Blend the tomatoes, chipotle peppers, and adobo sauce until mostly smooth.
  3. Cook the onion in a little oil 3-4 minutes until soft, then add garlic for 30 seconds.
  4. Pour in the tomato-chipotle sauce and chicken stock, simmering 8-10 minutes until thickened.
  5. Add the shredded chicken and stir to coat, simmering 5 more minutes.
  6. Taste and season with salt.
  7. Pile the tinga onto crisp tostadas.
  8. Top with shredded lettuce, sliced avocado, and crumbled queso fresco.

Carne Asada

25 min (+30 min marinate)EasyServes 1–4

Prep — Grilling the Marinated Steak

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Flank or skirt steak130g260g390g520g
Lime juice15ml30ml45ml60ml
Orange juice15ml30ml45ml60ml
Garlic cloves1234
Olive oil10ml20ml30ml40ml
Ground cumin⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Cilantro, chopped5g10g15g20g
White onion (for grilling)20g40g60g80g
Corn tortillas2468
Pico de gallo (side)30g60g90g120g

Steps

  1. Whisk together lime juice, orange juice, garlic, olive oil, cumin, and half the cilantro.
  2. Marinate the steak in the citrus mixture at least 30 minutes, up to 4 hours.
  3. Let the steak sit out 15 minutes before cooking so it isn't ice-cold.
  4. Heat a grill or grill pan over high heat until very hot.
  5. Grill the steak undisturbed 3-4 minutes per side until well marked.
  6. Flip once and cook 3-4 minutes more for medium doneness.
  7. Rest the steak 5-10 minutes before slicing.
  8. Slice thinly against the grain.
  9. Serve with warm tortillas, grilled onion, cilantro, and pico de gallo.

Pollo en Mole Poblano

55 minMediumServes 1–4

Prep — Toasting the Dried Chiles

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Chicken thighs130g260g390g520g
Dried ancho chiles1234
Dried pasilla chile½11½2
Roma tomato½11½2
Garlic cloves1234
White onion20g40g60g80g
Raisins5g10g15g20g
Almonds (or peanuts)5g10g15g20g
Sesame seeds5g10g15g20g
Mexican chocolate (or dark chocolate + cinnamon)10g20g30g40g
Chicken stock100ml200ml300ml400ml

Steps

  1. Toast the stemmed, seeded ancho and pasilla chiles in a dry pan 20-30 seconds per side.
  2. Soak the toasted chiles in boiling water 15 minutes until soft.
  3. Toast the almonds and sesame seeds separately until golden, setting a pinch of sesame aside for garnish.
  4. Cook the onion and garlic in a little oil until soft, then add tomato and cook until saucy.
  5. Blend the soaked chiles, toasted nuts and seeds, onion-tomato mixture, raisins, and half the stock until smooth.
  6. Cook the thick paste in a pot, stirring often, 5 minutes until darkened and toasty.
  7. Stir in the rest of the stock until the sauce is smooth and pourable.
  8. Add the chicken thighs, cover partway, and simmer 25-30 minutes until fully cooked.
  9. Melt the chocolate into the sauce and simmer 5 more minutes.
  10. Spoon over rice and sprinkle with the reserved toasted sesame seeds.

Churros with Mexican Chocolate Sauce (Bonus)

35 minEasyServes 1–4

Prep — Piping and Frying the Dough

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Water60ml120ml180ml240ml
Butter10g20g30g40g
Sugar (for dough)5g10g15g20g
Saltpinchpinch¼ tsp¼ tsp
All-purpose flour35g70g105g140g
Egg½11½2
Vegetable oil (for frying)250ml500ml750ml1000ml
Cinnamon sugar (for coating)15g30g45g60g
Mexican chocolate tablet (or dark chocolate)20g40g60g80g
Milk30ml60ml90ml120ml

Steps

  1. Bring water, butter, sugar, and salt to a boil until the butter melts.
  2. Off the heat, stir in all the flour at once until it forms a smooth dough ball.
  3. Let the dough cool about 5 minutes.
  4. Beat in the egg a little at a time until smooth and glossy.
  5. Pipe the dough into a piping bag fitted with a star tip.
  6. Heat the oil to about 190°C (375°F).
  7. Pipe 10-13cm lengths of dough directly into the hot oil, a few at a time.
  8. Fry 2-3 minutes per side until deep golden and crisp, then drain on paper towels.
  9. Roll the warm churros in cinnamon sugar.
  10. Warm the milk, stir in the chopped chocolate until melted, and serve alongside for dipping.
